slides.title: Memory Allocation Techniques
content: Memory management allocates and manages main memory to ensure efficient execution of processes
First Fit allocates the first available block that is large enough, making it fast but prone to fragmentation
Best Fit selects the smallest suitable block to minimize leftover space but requires more searching
Worst Fit chooses the largest block to leave large free spaces but may waste memory for small processes

slides.title: Contiguous Allocation, Paging, Segmentation
content: Contiguous allocation assigns a single continuous block of memory to a process, which is simple but causes external fragmentation :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}
Paging divides memory into fixed-size pages and frames, eliminating external fragmentation using page tables for mapping :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}
Segmentation divides memory into variable-sized logical segments like code, data, and stack, reflecting program structure :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}
Paging improves flexibility while segmentation improves logical organization but may cause fragmentation

slides.title: Virtual Memory & Page Fault
content: Virtual memory is a technique that uses disk storage to extend RAM, allowing programs larger than physical memory to execute :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}
It uses paging and page tables to map logical addresses to physical memory dynamically
A page fault occurs when a required page is not in memory and must be fetched from disk :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}
Frequent page faults can reduce performance and lead to excessive disk activity

slides.title: Page Replacement Algorithms
content: Page replacement algorithms decide which page to remove when memory is full to minimize page faults
FIFO replaces the oldest page first but may lead to inefficient performance and anomalies
LRU replaces the least recently used page based on past usage patterns for better performance
Optimal replaces the page that will not be used for the longest future time and provides the best theoretical performance

slides.title: Belady's Anomaly & Thrashing
content: Belady's anomaly occurs when increasing memory frames leads to more page faults, commonly seen in FIFO :contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}
Thrashing occurs when the system spends more time swapping pages than executing processes due to insufficient memory :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}
It leads to low CPU utilization, high disk activity, and poor system performance
It can be controlled using working set models and reducing multiprogramming levels

slides.title: Dynamic Binding
content: Dynamic binding resolves memory addresses at runtime instead of compile time for flexibility and efficient memory use :contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}
It allows programs to be loaded anywhere in memory and supports relocation during execution
It uses hardware like Memory Management Unit (MMU) for address translation
It improves flexibility but introduces runtime overhead and complexity
